courses.biggestGap: THE FLOOD — the named signature mechanic of an entire round of the cup — renders as a flat, static, untextured translucent quad with hard straight polygon edges laid on top of the tarmac, and no racer driving through it produces a single splash, spray plume or wake, so the player's only cue that they are in water is a colour shift.
courses.directive: Fix the flood surface on saltpan-bypass so a crossing reads as water, not as a coloured decal. Three specific things, in priority order: (1) the sheet's boundary is currently a hard straight polygon edge that cuts diagonally across the asphalt and, at the outer ends, floats above it with a visible vertical side wall — give it a soft alpha-dissolved margin plus a foam/wet band 1-2m wide, and conform it to the road surface so no lip is visible; (2) it is completely static — the surface has no motion, no ripple, no specular sparkle, so at 87 m/s it is indistinguishable from a painted patch; add a scrolling normal/UV animation driven off ctx.time (deterministic, no wall-clock); (3) most importantly, driving through it emits nothing — I captured five racers simultaneously inside the water with zero spray between them. Any racer whose sample().surface === 'water' must emit a persistent wheel-spray plume and a fading wake trail, the way the boost flame and drift spark systems already do. Item-strike sparks are currently the only white particles in frame while the field is submerged, which is why the crossing reads as an item pile-up rather than a flood. Second, smaller, same round of work: Switchback Summit is a 102m alpine mountain with no trees, bushes or vegetation of any kind — five metres past the kerb the world becomes a flat desaturated olive plane with a handful of tiny scatter props, and Mount Wario's equivalent moment is a dense pine forest.
evidence: Ran node tools/capture.mjs --only overhead,racing,far for all four courses (--course cone-canyon / jackhammer-quarry / saltpan-bypass / switchback-summit) and read every PNG.

Wrote a harness probe (reset{courseId}, setAutopilot, step 0.2s, snapshot) measuring one full lap per course: lap time 51.2 / 56.4 / 68.4 / 61.8s; elevation range 27.3 / 42.7 / 17.2 / 101.9m; longest continuous run above 95% of top speed 0.8 / 0.4 / 5.6 / 0.4s; surface histogram shows 'water' and 'sand' only on saltpan. The four courses are genuinely differentiated on geometry — this is not a re-skin roster, and the round-2 shape fix held.

Wrote a second harness script that steps saltpan-bypass until the player's sample().surface === 'water' and screenshots at 1280x720. inwater-0.png: five racers simultaneously inside the flood sheet, and there is not one splash, spray plume, droplet or wake anywhere in frame — the only white particles are item-strike spark rings. inwater-1.png: the cone is mid-crossing at speed, again producing zero spray; the flood is a flat teal translucent sheet whose near and far boundaries are hard straight lines ruled diagonally across the tarmac, with no foam, no wet margin and no surface motion.

perf.biggestGap: The governor writes the rung it settled on to localStorage and re-applies it on every future launch — I verified a reload booting straight into 0.50 render scale with FXAA off — while the product contains no graphics, quality, resolution or picture control anywhere, so a player downgraded by one busy launch cannot see that it happened, refuse it, or get their picture back.
perf.directive: Stop treating the stored rung as a standing answer, and get `qualityPref` a consumer. (1) In `core/quality.ts`, on boot restore at most half the remembered drop — clamp the start rung to `Math.ceil(remembered / 2)` — and make the governor re-earn the rest inside the first race, so one bad launch costs a player one race rather than every race thereafter. Today `hardwareKey`+`readMemory` restore rung 6 verbatim: I settled a session at the floor, reloaded, and `probe()` came back `{rung:6, scale:0.5, remembered:6}` off `localStorage["mc.quality.v1"]`. (2) `ctx.qualityPref` — which already publishes all seven rungs with labels, plus `rung`, `auto`, `remembered`, `set()` and `forget()` — is read by nothing in the repo: `grep -rn qualityPref src/` returns only `src/core/quality.ts` and `src/types.ts`, and scraping the live front-end's whole text finds MACHINE / CUP / CIRCUIT / CLASS / CONTROLS and no graphics row. Since you cannot edit `src/ui/**`, put an explicit cross-module request in your report for `ui/menus` (and the pause plate) to bind a PICTURE row to `qualityPref`, with `forget()` as the "my game looks worse than it used to" button. (3) Secondary, same file: your §8 futility stand-down never fires on the path the governor actually takes — 100s live at 31x over budget returned `verdicts: []`, `futile: 0`, because the six-rung prelude jump skips every rung the verdict machinery needs to measure; either accrue a verdict on the prelude jump itself or put the last rung back when `sessionMedianMs` stays above roughly `TARGET_MS * 1.43` after reaching the floor.
evidence: DOOR TEST (my own script, clean browser profile): boot reads {rung:0, label:'high', remembered:-1} — correct. 50s of live rAF play on this box → {rung:6, label:'floor', scale:0.5, remembered:6} and localStorage gains mc.quality.v1 = {"k":"ANGLE (Google, Vulkan 1.3.0 (SwiftShader...","rung":6}. Reload the page → boots at {rung:6, scale:0.5, prefAuto:true}. Persisted, silent, one-way.

NO DOOR: scraped every leaf text node of the live front-end — the entire visible product vocabulary is 'MACHINE / CUP / CIRCUIT / CLASS / HAZARD CUP / METRES / LAPS / TOTAL KM / CONTROLS' plus keycaps. No quality/graphics/resolution/detail control on the title screen, the select screens or the pause plate. `qualityPref` (rungs[7] with labels high…floor, set(), forget()) is referenced nowhere outside core/quality.ts and types.ts.

WHAT THE FLOOR RUNG LOOKS LIKE: zoomed the left guardrail 2x from a settled chase frame at rung 0 and at the floor. Rung 0 edges are clean; the floor shows hard 2px stair-stepping along the barrier top, the post silhouettes and the kerb line — 0.50 scale with FXAA off, upscaled, no resolve. Measured across the frame: world mean gradient 2.573 → 1.762 (-32%) while the HUD holds 6.661 → 6.657 bit-for-bit. Sharp HUD over a scaled world is the MK8D split-screen precedent and is fine; 800x450 stretched to 1600x900 with no AA is worse than any mode MK8 ships.
